text:
Rethink Technology business briefs for January 24, 2018.
Canalys says Apple sold 29 million iPhone Xs in December quarter 
Source: Canalys 
Rumors that the latest iPhone has flopped or not met expectations have become a staple of Apple ( AAPL ) coverage in the run-up to its all-important December quarter earnings report. This year is no exception. Research firm Canalys threw some much needed cold water on reports yesterday when it issued a report claiming that Apple had shipped 29 million iPhone Xs in its fiscal 2018 Q1, ending in December.
The number is really stunning when one considers that it's probably comparable to the number of iPhone 7s sold in the December 2016 quarter. I base this on the fact that Apple reported selling 78.29 million iPhones worldwide in the December 2016 quarter.
If CIRP's data , shown below, for the US last year is globally applicable, then about 40% of total unit shipments, or 31 million, were iPhone 7. The global product mix might be different from the US mix that CIRP determined, but I think the US mix is fairly representative.
The mathematical implication of the Canalys number is even more stunning when combined with the CIRP product mix data. If 29 million iPhone Xs constitute about 20% of global sales, then Apple sold 145 million iPhones in the December quarter, for a y/y gain of 85%.
